scope: Large saved task-recovery draft preparation in both independent apps; existing recovery validators, cache contents/order and export contract retained.

core.coverage: 10,000 unrelated cached tasks/101 authored records/102 queue commands; full 50,000-row capacity; combined 50,000-row/1,000-command capacity including every historical note; full queue and surviving order preservation, exact separate/combined outputs, captured discussion/cancellation phases, and invalid envelope refusal.

performance.baselineOrigin: iOS-owned Core source before optimization on this Mac
performance.survivingCacheOrder: Explicit full ordered-ID equality per case; iOS medium hash also matches the separately captured old-path result. Maximum queue and row-only cases retain identical task order.
performance.limits: Observed synthetic debug samples, not controlled release/hardware performance guarantees. Concurrent suites/compilers affect timing; elapsed time is not a test assertion.

contract.model: Immutable derived content shared by text/export. No persisted cache or new Codable fields. Task indexing keeps first-match semantics.
contract.replay: Every row and existing validator retained. Only the private draft-analysis copy places the affected cohort first. Returned initial workspace is independently constructed in original cache order; ordinary acknowledgement is unchanged.
contract.authority: Prepared content never authorizes recovery. Existing current read/session/workspace guards remain; preservation still requires the existing backup/encrypted archive/proof/persist sequence.
contract.exports: Original task/command/conversation histories retained; unrelated cache, permission snapshot and synthetic analysis state excluded.

native.build: Current signed app/test targets pass; strict signature and namespace-only prepared-source checks pass.

remaining: Mac UI approval and native acceptance
Maximum-size interactive and archive-I/O acceptance; broader spoken/recurring/hosted checks
Provisional connected-copy cohorts and unsupported legacy discussion context
I/O-phase account/session UI races and genuine hosted team acceptance before default-off rollout; user deferrals unchanged
